Adjacent columns are sampled at different MOMENTS OF THE FOOTAGE, so the clip's own frame rate is what ripples — the bed never moves. The shear knob is headWidth*source.rate/(advance*60) = 8*2/240 = 0.067 source-seconds between columns, about a frame and a half: enough to ripple, not enough to smear. FRAMES 16 IS WHAT MAKES IT A VIDEO RATHER THAN A WIPE: every column holds 16 instants and playback advances all of them at once, so the picture moves with the head standing still. At frames 1 there is no stack, nothing to play, and the only recordable thing is the sweep laying the tape down — which is a recording of the process, not of the result. WANTS A CONTINUOUS SHOT: one wrap spends 8 seconds of footage, so a clip that cuts inside that window gives a collage of different shots instead of one undulating picture. Too subtle: raise source.rate toward 3-4. Too violent: drop it toward 1.5. Costs 16 strip draws per step — on a software renderer that is slow.
